title: Classical deductions for equality-free signed formulas

based_on.title: Proof Theory 2018: Syntax and semantics of predicate logic; Natural Deduction (handout 8)
Proof Theory 2018: Sequent calculus for predicate logic (handout 9)

summary: Convert actual classical deductions between full equality-free formulas and their positive or negative signed readings, preserving contexts and temporary names.
abstract: Moving a negation through a universal quantifier changes it into an existential claim about a counterexample. Classical deductions must explain how to produce that conclusion while keeping a temporary witness separate from the assumptions. We construct proof conversions for this step and for every other connective, obtaining the specified signed normal form of an equality-free formula. Both directions act on supplied finite deduction trees and preserve their allowed assumptions. Signed duality then becomes provable primitive negation, and the same conversions work with an auxiliary reserve in languages without constants.
